about.title: About this shop
about.tagline: A complete e-commerce storefront that sells nothing — on purpose.
intro: This is a demo shop. Every product, price, order and customer in it is seeded data, put here so you can walk through a real storefront end to end: find a product, save it, put it in the cart, check out with an address and a shipping method, then watch the order move through its statuses. No payment is ever taken and nothing ships.

It exists to show what the boilerplate underneath can do. The catalogue is small on purpose — small enough that you can see stock go down when you buy, a category chip filter the list, and an order you placed a minute ago get cancelled.
Everything you click calls the same API a real deployment would. The errors are real too: order more than the shelf holds and you get the exact message a paying customer would see.

catalogue.title: Browse the catalogue
catalogue.text: Search, filter by category, open a product page and see its live stock. Admins add and edit products from the same screens.

wishlist.title: Save for later
wishlist.text: The heart on a product keeps it on your wishlist; move it to the cart in one click when you are ready.

cart.title: Cart and checkout
cart.text: Quantities capped by what is in stock, a saved address, a shipping method priced against your lines — and a server that re-checks all of it before it places the order.

orders.title: Order history
orders.text: Every order you place, its payment, its parcel and its status timeline. Cancel one while it is pending, or reorder it back into the cart.

account.title: Your account
account.text: Sign up with an email, edit your profile and picture, change your password, reset it when you forget it, and delete the account when you are done.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.text: A contact form whose messages land in an admin inbox on this very site, where each one moves through its statuses.

languages.title: Two languages
languages.text: English and Italian, switchable from the header — and translators can edit either dictionary live from the admin side.

theme.title: Light and dark
theme.text: Follows your system by default; one click pins the theme you prefer.

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.text: Vue 3 with Vuetify and Tailwind, Pinia stores, vue-router with locale-prefixed routes, vue-i18n dictionaries.

api.title: API
api.text: A Node.js and MongoDB backend, with a demo profile that boots on an in-memory database and seeds the data you see.

contract.title: One contract
contract.text: An OpenAPI document shared by both sides: the client, its types and the response validators are generated from it, so the two cannot drift.

realtime.title: Realtime
realtime.text: Server-sent events and a WebSocket channel, typed from an AsyncAPI document the same way.

quality.title: Quality gates
quality.text: Unit tests, end-to-end tests, visual regression, accessibility sweeps and mutation testing, all in the repository.

observability.title: Observability
observability.text: Health, metrics and an audit log on an admin console; errors and web vitals reported from the browser.

try.title: Take it for a spin
steps: Browse the catalogue and open a product — notice its stock count.
Sign up with any email you like; nothing is sent to it.
Add a few products to the cart, then try ordering more of one than the shelf holds.
Check out with a saved address and a shipping method, then open the order and watch it progress.
Send a message through the contact form — an admin will find it in the inbox.
try.note: The data resets from time to time, so do not keep anything here you would miss — and please do not enter real personal details.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.intro: The questions a demo shop gets asked — about shopping here, about your orders and account, and about the demo itself.

entries.q: How do I find a product?
entries.a: Open the catalogue from the header and use the search box or the category chips to narrow the list. Every product has its own page with a description, a price and its current stock.

entries.q: What does the stock number mean?
entries.a: It is the live count from the shop's inventory ledger: every purchase takes from it and every cancellation gives back. One product is always out of stock on purpose — a shop where nothing is ever scarce cannot show you what happens at checkout when something is.

entries.q: Can I save a product for later?
entries.a: Yes. The heart on a product page adds it to your wishlist, which needs an account. From the wishlist you can move an item straight into the cart.

Add a product from its page and adjust the quantity in the cart; you cannot go above what is in stock. The cart lives on the server, so it follows your account across devices, and the header always shows how many units it holds and what they add up to.

From the cart, pick one of your saved addresses and a shipping method, then place the order. The server checks stock and prices again at that moment: if anything changed since you loaded the page, the cart refreshes and asks you to review it before trying again.
No. The payment panel on each order simulates a payment provider so you can see the flow — nothing is charged and no card details are ever asked for.
No. Shipping methods are real enough to be priced against your cart, and each order shows a parcel panel with its status, but no physical shipment exists.

entries.q: Can I cancel or repeat an order?
entries.a: You can cancel an order while it is still pending, from its page. Reorder copies its lines back into your cart; a product that has since left the catalogue is skipped and you are told so.
Browsing is open to everyone. The wishlist, the cart, checkout and the order history are yours, so they need you to be signed in.
Use the link on the sign-in page: it walks you through a reset request and a confirmation, the same flow a real shop would run.
Yes, from your profile. The deletion asks you to confirm before anything is removed.
It is demo data on a demo server, reset from time to time. Please do not enter real personal details; the privacy page explains what is stored and why.
No. Products, prices, orders and customers are seeded demo data; no payment is ever taken and nothing ships.

entries.q: Can I use this code for my own shop?
entries.a: Yes: it is a boilerplate. Replace the seed data, the copy on these pages and the theme, and the rest is yours to keep or delete — each domain is a module you can remove in one go.

entries.q: Where do my contact messages go?
entries.a: Into the admin inbox on this very site. Sign in as an admin and you can move each message through its statuses.

entries.q: What is on the admin side?
entries.a: Users, products and orders management, the inventory ledger, the translations editor, the feedback inbox, and an observability console with health, metrics and an audit log.
English and Italian, switchable from the header. Translators can edit either dictionary live from the admin side, and the change shows up without a deployment.

contact.text: Send it through the contact form — it lands in the admin inbox.

paragraphs: Analytics: when it is configured, this site measures pageviews with a self-hosted Umami tracker, but only after you accept the analytics banner. That includes the address of each page, your browser language and screen size, and the page you came from. Decline, or withdraw from "Privacy choices" in the footer, and the tracker does not load or stops sending. If you are signed in, your account id is attached to what is recorded.

Crash reports and page speed: when it is configured, this site sends errors, console errors, how fast pages load and a trace of each request to its own collector (Grafana Faro, run by the operator, not a third party), but only after you accept the same banner. That includes the address of each page without anything after a ? or #, your browser, operating system, language and screen size, and your IP address as the collector receives it. If you are signed in and accepted, your account id is attached. Decline, or withdraw, and nothing is sent. One key, com.grafana.faro.lastNavigationId, is kept in sessionStorage until you close the tab.

browser-storage.title: Cookies and storage
browser-storage.intro: Everything this site leaves in your browser. Items marked strictly necessary keep you signed in, keep your cart or remember a choice you made, so they do not need your consent.
browser-storage.turnstile: The human check on some forms is Cloudflare Turnstile, a third party: it loads a script from Cloudflare and Cloudflare sees your visit to that form.

session.purpose: Keeps you signed in. The shop reads it on every request; script on the page cannot.
session.lifetime: While you stay signed in: the browser session, or 30 days if you ticked “Remember me”

isAuth.purpose: A hint that you were signed in, so the page can show the right menu before the first answer arrives. It holds no credential.
isAuth.lifetime: As long as the session cookie

rememberMe.purpose: Records that you ticked “Remember me” at sign-in.

device.purpose: Lets a browser you already signed in from keep signing in while someone else is guessing your password. Holds one signed token per account.

oauthState.purpose: Protects a sign-in with an outside provider against forgery.

oauthVerifier.purpose: Proves it is the same browser that started a sign-in with an outside provider.

oauthContinue.purpose: Remembers the page to return to after signing in with an outside provider.

oauthLocale.purpose: Remembers your language across a sign-in with an outside provider.

oauthLink.purpose: Remembers that you are linking a provider to your signed-in account.

oauthMfaChallenge.purpose: Carries the second-step check of a sign-in with an outside provider.
oauthMfaChallenge.lifetime: As long as the check stays open, at most a few minutes

themePreference.purpose: Remembers whether you chose the light or the dark look.

analyticsConsent.purpose: Remembers your answer to the analytics banner.
analyticsConsent.lifetime: 6 months, then you are asked again

toursSeen.purpose: Remembers which guided tours were already shown in this browser.

guestCart.purpose: Keeps the cart you built before signing in, in this browser only.

guestCartMergeAttempt.purpose: Finishes moving your cart into your account if the page was closed halfway.

checkoutDraft.purpose: Keeps what you typed at checkout if the page reloads.

checkoutAttempt.purpose: Stops a checkout you retry from placing the order twice.

staleDeployReloaded.purpose: Stops the page from reloading itself more than once after a new version went online.

umamiDisabled.purpose: The analytics tracker’s own “do not send” switch, set when you decline or withdraw.

faroNavigation.purpose: Used by the performance-measurement library to tell one page load from the next. Set only after you accept analytics.
